title: HIDRA – Study on the prediction of intraoperative hypotension in women undergoing spinal anesthesia during cesarean section using perfusion index, pulse transit time, RR interval, and changes in pulse wave morphology
summary:
During a cesarean section, spinal anesthesia is administered to prevent pain. This anesthesia can cause a sharp drop in blood pressure in many women, triggering nausea, vomiting, or dizziness. Blood pressure is measured with a cuff that only takes intermittent readings, resulting in gaps in monitoring. Other values, such as oxygen saturation and heart rate, are recorded continuously. We are investigating whether these values—such as the perfusion index, heart rhythm, or pulse waves—can predict a drop in blood pressure and fill in the gaps to provide help more quickly.
In this study, we analyze simple vital signs such as the perfusion index or pulse transit time, which are measured during your surgery anyway, in order to detect a drop in blood pressure at an early stage. Anesthesia practice remains unchanged; the study has no influence on your current treatment. Our goal is to use this analysis to improve patient care in the future so that complications become less frequent.
In summary:
Objective: We want to find out whether simple measurements such as perfusion index, pulse transit time, heartbeat intervals, or pulse waveform can predict a drop in blood pressure early on during a cesarean section with spinal anesthesia.
Method: We only use the usual measurements (e.g., blood pressure, pulse) that are taken during your surgery anyway, without any extra equipment or procedures.
Procedure: Your data will be evaluated anonymously, without affecting your treatment; there will be no additional visits or tasks for you.

interventions.name: Women undergoing elective C-Section under spinal anesthesia. Analysis of routine perioperative vital signs with empahsis on Perfusion Index, RR-Interval, and PPG Pulse Wave morphology.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
The inclusion criteria for this study are as follows: Adult women aged 18 years or older who are undergoing a cesarean section under primary spinal anesthesia for a duration of at least 30 minutes.
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria: Cesarean section under general anesthesia, cesarean section with epidural catheter, congenital heart defects, atrial fibrillation or other arrhythmias, emergency cesarean section.
